exposure: Type of anesthesia in cesarean delivery (spinal vs. general)
Mode of birth (vaginal vs. cesarean section)
cohort: The study included pregnant women admitted to the hospital with confirmed COVID-19 who gave birth during hospitalization between March 2020 and November 2021.
finding: The clinical severity of COVID-19 and changes in clinical status were the critical factors influencing the method and timing of birth and negative outcomes for pregnant women with COVID-19.
mod_finding: Cesarean birth was associated with a higher preterm birth rate (<34 weeks) compared to vaginal birth (OR 2.311, 95% CI 1.155-4.625).
